key_insight: Trials with English-language eligibility requirements enrolled fewer Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants, while language accommodation was uncommon.
clinical_relevance: Adding explicit language accommodations to trial criteria could be a practical way to improve representation in US clinical trial enrollment.
method: Cross-sectional analysis of ClinicalTrials.gov interventional trials with at least one US site and posted results.
Eligibility criteria were mined with regular expressions to detect English-language requirements and language accommodations.
Associations with enrolled race/ethnicity proportions were modeled with adjustments for trial and site characteristics.
evidence_signal: In 44,487 US-only trials, an English-language requirement appeared in 12.9% and was associated with lower enrolled proportions of Asian and Hispanic/Latinx participants; language accommodation was documented in only 1.8% of trials.
watch_item: This is an observational registry study, so the associations do not prove causation and may be influenced by incomplete race/ethnicity reporting in some trials.
paper_title: Language eligibility criteria and enrolled racial and ethnic composition in US clinical trials: a cross-sectional study
